titulo: The seven pieces of a Jarvis
lead: Every agent, from the simplest to the most expensive, has the same seven pieces: a door, a heart, an identity, a brain, a memory, hands, and a vault. If you know the pieces, you choose better, spend less, and don't get locked into one product. INTELECTO is our example: small on purpose, so you can read it.
objetivo: explain the path of a message and say, for each of the seven pieces, what it does and where it sits in INTELECTO.

aprende.t: The path of a message, from Telegram to the model and back
What each of the seven pieces does
Why the loop with a brake sets an agent apart from a chatbot
How contracts let you swap one piece without touching the rest

hero_alt: Seven wooden blocks on a table, each with an object: a phone, a gear, a card, a chip, a drawer, a key, and a padlock.

secoes.sub: Scroll the page: each step lights up one piece.

nos.detalhe: This is where you talk to it. In INTELECTO, that's Telegram: one token and you're set, with no public address on the internet. The agent asks Telegram whether a new message has arrived, splits replies longer than 4,000 characters, and shows "typing" while it thinks.

It receives the message, thinks, uses a tool if it needs to, looks at the result, and thinks again, until it answers with text. It has a brake: at most five tool rounds per message. Past that, it has to answer.

Four simple files in the workspace folder: the soul, the rules, your profile, and the starting facts. With every message, the agent reads all four. Change the text, change the assistant, no programming.
The AI model. In the cloud, OpenRouter: one key gives you access to more than a hundred models. On your own computer, Ollama: no cost per message and nothing sent outside.
It stores what matters in a SQLite database on your machine, with word search and no API cost. With every message, it looks up what's relevant and puts it in the context.

Without tools it only talks; with them it gets things done. At the core: read and write files, list a folder, run commands, save to and search memory. Each tool describes itself, and the model reads that description to decide whether to use it.
API keys that are encrypted and tied to the machine, a list of forbidden commands, a 60-second time limit per command, and an audit log of everything it ran.

secoes.volta: The reply travels back through the channel to your phone
secoes.legenda: The same seven pieces show up in INTELECTO, in OpenClaw, in Hermes, or in a Jarvis you build yourself.

rolagem_fim.texto: You write on Telegram. The loop gathers identity and memory, sends them to the model, runs the tool it asks for, within the vault's limits, and the reply comes back through the same channel.

secoes.titulo: Three ideas that hold the pieces together

texto: INTELECTO is a personal assistant for one owner. It is not multi-user, doesn't depend on the cloud, doesn't need Docker, has no web dashboard, and isn't a black box.
The plan calls for about three thousand lines and seven dependencies: you can read it all.

exemplo.texto: Can I explain what happens between my message and the reply? If not, it's a black box.

texto: A chatbot answers and forgets. An agent thinks, acts with a tool, looks at the result, and thinks again.
With no ceiling, an agent can keep spinning and spending without finishing. That's why the five-round brake.

exemplo.texto: At most 5 tool rounds per message; after that, reply with text.

texto: Each piece is defined by a contract: the channel has start, send, and stop; the provider receives the conversation and the tools and returns the response.
Want WhatsApp instead of Telegram, or Ollama instead of OpenRouter? It's another file with the same contract.

exemplo.texto: New tool = new file in the same pattern. The registry finds it on its own, with no changes to the core.

texto: The features guide organizes everything into eight corridors: identity, security, channels, memory, automation, integrations, skills, and architecture.
You don't need everything. Scheduling and web search, for example, are in the plan for the next phase.

exemplo.texto: Loop + a brain + a channel + a basic SOUL. Memory comes right after.

secoes.sub: The core tree that the agent builds in the repository example.

blocos.conteudo:
jarvis/
  channels/    # the door: terminal and Telegram
  agent/       # the heart: loop.py and context.py
  providers/   # the brain: contract + test model
  memory/      # the memory: SQLite with search
  tools/       # the hands: files, command, memory
  security/    # the vault: secrets and block list
workspace/
  SOUL.md  AGENTS.md  USER.md  MEMORY.md   # the identity

| Piece       | What it does (in my own words)     | Where it lives |
|-------------|------------------------------------|----------------|
| Channel     |                                    |                |
| Loop        |                                    |                |
| Identity    |                                    |                |
| Brain       |                                    |                |
| Memory      |                                    |                |
| Tools       |                                    |                |
| Vault       |                                    |                |

abas.html:
1. You write on Telegram.
  2. The channel receives it and hands it to the loop.
  3. The loop builds the context: SOUL + AGENTS + USER and the relevant memories.
  4. The model answers or asks for a tool; the loop runs it and returns the result (up to 5 rounds).
  5. The answer goes back through the channel.

Chatbot: answers, forgets when the conversation ends, has no identity, takes no action, doesn't know you.

Jarvis: remembers past conversations, has a written name and values, uses tools, and knows your context.

secoes.sub: Before you build, understand what you're going to build.

perguntas.p: What makes an agent more than just a chatbot?
opcoes: The loop: think, use a tool, look at the result, and think again until it answers.
perguntas.explica: The loop is what turns conversation into action. The model can be the same; what changes is being able to use tools and look at the result before answering.

perguntas.p: What is the five-round tool limit for?
opcoes: It's the brake: without it, the agent can keep spinning and spending without ever finishing.
perguntas.explica: The cap forces the agent to answer after five rounds. A short, readable loop with a cap is what separates a useful agent from one that spends nonstop.

perguntas.p: You want to swap Telegram for WhatsApp. What changes?
opcoes: A new channel file that fulfills the same contract (start, send, stop); everything else stays the same.
You have to rewrite the whole agent.
It can't be done: INTELECTO only speaks Telegram.
You also have to switch models.
perguntas.explica: Each piece is a contract. A new channel implements the same three functions and the loop doesn't even notice the swap.

perguntas.p: Where does the assistant's personality live?
opcoes: In four text files in the workspace folder.
perguntas.explica: SOUL, AGENTS, USER, and MEMORY are plain text. The agent reads all four with every message: change the text, change the assistant.
